classify_ltv's LOW-band boundary comparison currently uses the strict '<' operator against thresholds.ltv_low_max.basis_points, so an ltv value exactly equal to ltv_low_max does NOT satisfy the LOW branch and falls through to the MEDIUM check.

findings.claim: The established convention within classify_dti and classify_ltv themselves (their own MEDIUM-boundary comparisons, which are not regressed) is: a value exactly equal to a band's own upper threshold belongs to that (lower-numbered) band, expressed with the '<=' operator against that threshold. This is confirmed both by the current, correct MEDIUM-band lines in the same functions and by the pre-regression diff, which shows the LOW-band comparisons originally used '<=' in exactly the same style before being changed to '<'.

findings.claim: classify_credit_score, in the same file, follows a different (but internally consistent) boundary style from classify_dti/classify_ltv: it uses strict '<' comparisons at each ascending threshold (300<=score<=850 validated first; then score<580 POOR, score<670 FAIR, score<740 GOOD, else EXCELLENT), under which a boundary value (e.g. exactly 580 or 670 or 740) belongs to the NEXT/higher bucket rather than the lower one. This is the opposite inclusion direction from classify_dti/classify_ltv's own MEDIUM-boundary convention (F-5), so classify_credit_score is not the correct model to copy for the LOW-boundary comparisons in classify_dti/classify_ltv -- the correct model is those two functions' own existing MEDIUM-boundary lines (F-5).

findings.claim: demo-repo/tests/unit/test_risk_profile.py exercises build_risk_profile with dti/ltv inputs that are not exactly equal to dti_low_max or ltv_low_max (e.g. income $10,000/debt $500, loan $150,000/collateral $300,000), so none of its three tests independently exercise or currently fail on the LOW-boundary regression in classify_dti/classify_ltv.

build_risk_profile's overall_band is susceptible to the same LOW-boundary misclassification as classify_dti/classify_ltv themselves: because build_risk_profile directly consumes classify_dti's and classify_ltv's return values with no additional boundary logic of its own, an applicant whose computed dti or ltv lands exactly at dti_low_max or ltv_low_max would have overall_band incorrectly elevated to MEDIUM under the current regressed code -- but no existing test in test_risk_profile.py currently exercises or catches that exact-boundary case.
findings.reasoning: F-7 establishes that build_risk_profile's overall_band is a direct, unmodified function of classify_dti's and classify_ltv's Band outputs (via _BAND_WEIGHT) with no independent boundary re-check. F-8 establishes that none of test_risk_profile.py's existing tests use inputs that land exactly on dti_low_max/ltv_low_max. Combining these: the LOW-boundary regression in classify_dti/classify_ltv would propagate into overall_band for an applicant at that exact boundary, but this propagation is not directly observed in any test evidence, so it is inferred rather than found.
